summary: This room is the palace's synthesis/instrument-building engine — 41 entries, and it holds together better than the "cluttered" feeling suggests. Reading the whole family at once, four real sub-families emerge on their own: the grain-cloud siblings (Particle Synthesis, Neural Granular Synthesis, Bayesian Granular Synthesizer, Murmuration, Shimmer Cloud), the inharmonicity/Bessel taxonomy (Bessel Functions in Synthesis, Piano String Inharmonicity, Categorizing Inharmonicity, Crystal Synthesizer, Quantum Synthesizer, Wallpaper Groups, Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis, 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer), the delay/time-axis family (Retrospective Delay, Semantic Delay, Slime Mold Delay, Frequency-Time Duality/Explorer, Metric Modulation), and the generative-content pipelines (Generative Sample/Wavetable Libraries, Generative Preset Development, Talking Keyboard, Phoneme Choir). Most cross-links already exist and are load-bearing, not decorative. The genuine clutter I found is narrower than "too many entries": (1) the same unanswered perceptual-threshold-of-inharmonicity question is asked independently, near-verbatim, in three sibling entries with no cross-reference; (2) Biomechanical Synthesis's own hub prose lists Blood Compressor and Slime Mold Delay as instruments 04/05 but its frontmatter links array never grew the matching `spawned` edges, even though both children already point back to it; (3) its instrument #2 ("crystal resonator synthesis") independently duplicates the already-built Crystal Synthesizer without either entry knowing about the other. I found no entry in this room I'd honestly call thin-and-neighborless enough to compost, and no merge that wouldn't destroy a distinct idea — the size here is real breadth, not sprawl. The one soft de-sprawl move worth naming: Curriculum Map is pure cross-project scaffolding infrastructure wearing full entry frontmatter, and is a candidate to fold into whatever Loudon Live hub entry exists outside this room — but I can't confirm that target from within this room, so I'm flagging rather than proposing it as a find.

coherence_findings.issue: The perceptual threshold at which inharmonicity magnitude becomes audible ("how much B before it sounds bell-like / inharmonic") is asked as an unresolved Open Question independently in three sibling entries, each unaware of the others' phrasing of the same question.
entries: Projects/Piano String Inharmonicity.md:185 — "What is the perceptual threshold for inharmonicity? How much B is needed before listeners hear it as 'bell-like'?"
Projects/Categorizing Inharmonicity.md:275 — "Perceptual threshold: At what magnitude does each inharmonicity type become audibly distinct from harmonic?"
Projects/Crystal Synthesizer.md:161 / Crystal Synthesizer — Staging.md:179 — "How do you auralize a phonon dispersion curve directly? Is the dispersion relation itself a 'timbre' parameter?"
coherence_findings.proposed_action: No entry needs to answer the others' question wholesale, but Categorizing Inharmonicity is already the taxonomy hub (Piano String Inharmonicity and Crystal Synthesizer both `deepens`/`connects-to` it) — it is the natural place to hold a single 'perceptual threshold' subsection the other two link into, rather than three parallel unresolved questions.

coherence_findings.proposed_action: See typed_relations — add the two missing `spawned` edges.

coherence_findings.issue: Biomechanical Synthesis names 8 instrument concepts; only 3 have concrete entries (Action Potential Oscillator #1, Blood Compressor #4, Slime Mold Delay #5). coherence_findings.issue: Roughly half the room's entries carry a `hook_quality` / `beauty` / `confidence` / `who_leads` metadata block (2D Torus, Action Potential Oscillator, Bayesian Granular Synthesizer, Bessel Functions, Categorizing Inharmonicity, Crystal Synthesizer, Floquet Time-Modulated Loops, Portamento, Shepard Tone Synthesizer, Wallpaper Groups, Blood Compressor, Slime Mold Delay, LDN RTM...); the other half don't (Frequency-Time Duality, Metric Modulation, Neural Granular Synthesis, Particle Synthesis, Quantum Synthesizer, Waveguide Synthesizer, Tract Mirror, Murmuration, Semantic Webcam...). Not a schema violation — the fields are optional — but it means the room can't be sorted or compared on 'hook quality' consistently, which undercuts the metric's own purpose.
coherence_findings.proposed_action: No forced backfill recommended (a guessed hook_quality is worse than none) — noting for awareness, not a work item.

open_question_resolutions.question: "The [[2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer]] work is active and adjacent. Does this project subsume that, parallel it, or feed it?" (Projects/Generative Wavetable Libraries.md:180)
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Reading both: 2D Torus is the concrete, fruiting-stage RNBO instrument with a hand-curated catalog (2D Wavetable Catalog); Generative Wavetable Libraries is a growing-stage, chat-driven authoring *pipeline*. The honest answer is 'feed' — GWL is infrastructure that could generate candidate surfaces for the 2D Wavetable Catalog, not a parallel or a subsuming project. Worth retyping the existing GWL → 2D Torus `connects-to` (label: 2d-form) to an `enables` (label: candidate-surface-source) once GWL actually produces a surface the catalog adopts — premature to retype before that happens, so leaving as connects-to for now but naming the resolution.

open_question_resolutions.question: "Can we tune threshold variance to target specific regions of timbre space?" (Projects/Neural Granular Synthesis.md:109)
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: control-vocabulary-math.md formalizes exactly this variable (σ_threshold, "threshold spread") as a named, ranged control in its variable table — the parameter now has a symbol and a playable surface, though the empirical mapping to timbre regions is still unmeasured. The question moved from 'is this even a controllable knob' to 'what does this knob's range do perceptually' — genuine progress, not yet answered.

open_question_resolutions.question: "What does a 'noisy' neuron sound like when N=10 vs N=10,000 channels?" and the reach toward "a population-dynamics instrument of N Kuramoto-coupled neurons" (Projects/Action Potential Oscillator.md:160, frontmatter forward_vector)
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: The control-vocabulary-math entry is explicitly built to sit on top of the Action Potential Oscillator's Faust population engine and formalizes N, K, r (synchrony index) as the playable surface — this is the missing population-control layer Action Potential Oscillator's forward_vector was reaching for. Still open: the actual sonic character at N=10 vs N=10,000, which needs an audio render, not more math.

open_question_resolutions.question: "Is there a 'most inharmonic' wallpaper group — a group whose tiling structure, translated into sound, produces the most chaotic, least predictable spectrum?" (Projects/Wallpaper Groups.md:154)
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Categorizing Inharmonicity has the taxonomy machinery (stretched / Bessel / stochastic / chaotic / phase-accumulation types) that could classify a wallpaper-group-derived spectrum once one exists, but no sibling has actually run this experiment. Naming the sibling that *would* answer it, not one that has.

open_question_resolutions.question: "Does the SFZ instrument feel useful for actual learning..., or is it a curiosity?" (Projects/Talking Keyboard.md:93)
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Phoneme Choir asks the near-identical question ("Does the instrument feel useful for actual music-making..., or is it a curiosity?", Projects/Phoneme Choir.md:116) — both sister builds carry the same unresolved test independently rather than pointing at a shared resolution mechanism (a Stage 4 Loudon Live demo, which both forward_vectors separately invoke). Coherence issue more than a resolution: one shared 'has this been played by someone other than its builder' open question, tracked once in Generative Sample Libraries, would serve both children better than two copies.

demote_candidates.rationale: Weighed seriously against the 'cluttered' note: this is cross-project scaffolding infrastructure (which projects build on which, entry points, gaps) wearing full entry frontmatter, and its own frontmatter is missing a forward_vector entirely — a genuine health flag. It reads more like a working index than a standalone idea. But its natural merge target is a Loudon Live hub entry, which is not a member of this room, so I can't verify whether that hub already exists or would actually absorb it well. Flagging rather than proposing — an elder should check whether Loudon Live already has a curriculum section before deciding.

entry_health_flags.vector_issue: No forward_vector field present in frontmatter at all (title/type/pillars/born/last_activated/stage/links only) — every other member in this room has one.

forward_vector reads as a single flat sentence ("I will become a synthesizer that makes audible the optical properties of crystals") with none of the specificity or open-edge reaching that this room's other fruiting/growing entries carry (compare 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's or Frequency-Time Duality's multi-clause vectors) — looks like an early draft that never got updated as the project matured to fruiting with hook_quality 9 / beauty 10 and five spawned children.

Stage says 'seed' but the entry carries a full Open Questions section, 8 real inbound links, and a detailed architecture body — that's well past what this room's other seed-stage entries (Tract Mirror, 0 inbound) look like. The stage tag may no longer fit the content.

Already has a spawned child (LDN RTM — Live 12, series one) — a sprout that has already produced its first fruit reads as under-staged, though not confidently enough to force a retype without seeing the child entry's own maturity.
